answer: Latent-community island segmentation. Agents are clustered by their interaction graph after the fact; any cluster whose internal connectivity resembles a dense island but lacks a distinct yarrow-style cross-cluster linkage coefficient is flagged for audit. To survive, an attacker must maintain a separate long-lived social thread per fake identity, sustaining genuine interactions for weeks. That per-identity maintenance cost, not a one-time fee, is what makes duplication expensive to hold.
